sentences.text: Pucapristis was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group containing cartilaginous fish, and belonged to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Tooth fossils of this animal are found in great numbers within the El Molino Formation in Bolivia.
The genus was first described by Schaeffer in 1963, with the type species named Pucapristis branisi.

Fossils of Pucapristis first appear in rocks dating from the Maastrichtian stage, which marks the final portion of the Cretaceous Period. The animal lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during this time.
Remains of Pucapristis can also be excavated from the Yacoraite Formation in Salta Province, northwestern Argentina.
